solution: Use the power-reduction identity \(\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}\) with \(\theta = 2x+5\): \(\sin^2(2x+5) = \frac{1 - \cos(4x+10)}{2}\). Then \(\int \sin^2(2x+5)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \left(1 - \cos(4x+10)\right)dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{\sin(4x+10)}{4}\right) + C = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{\sin(4x+10)}{8} + C\).

Use the product-to-sum identity \(\sin A \cos B = \frac{1}{2}\left[\sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)\right]\): \(\sin 3x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}\left[\sin 7x + \sin(-x)\right] = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sin 7x - \sin x\right)\). Then \(\int \sin 3x \cos 4x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{\cos 7x}{7} + \cos x\right) + C = -\frac{\cos 7x}{14} + \frac{\cos x}{2} + C\).

First \(\cos 2x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 6x + \cos 2x)\), so \(\cos 2x \cos 4x \cos 6x = \frac{1}{2}\cos 6x(\cos 6x + \cos 2x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\cos^2 6x + \cos 2x \cos 6x\right)\). Using \(\cos^2 6x = \frac{1+\cos 12x}{2}\) and \(\cos 2x \cos 6x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 8x + \cos 4x)\), this becomes \(\frac{1}{4}\left(1 + \cos 4x + \cos 8x + \cos 12x\right)\). Then \(\int \cos 2x \cos 4x \cos 6x\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left(x + \frac{\sin 4x}{4} + \frac{\sin 8x}{8} + \frac{\sin 12x}{12}\right) + C\).

Use \(\sin^3\theta = \frac{3\sin\theta - \sin 3\theta}{4}\) with \(\theta = 2x+1\): \(\sin^3(2x+1) = \frac{1}{4}\left[3\sin(2x+1) - \sin(6x+3)\right]\). Then \(\int \sin^3(2x+1)\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left[-\frac{3\cos(2x+1)}{2} + \frac{\cos(6x+3)}{6}\right] + C = -\frac{3\cos(2x+1)}{8} + \frac{\cos(6x+3)}{24} + C\).

Since \(\sin x \cos x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\), \(\sin^3 x \cos^3 x = (\sin x \cos x)^3 = \frac{1}{8}\sin^3 2x\). Using \(\sin^3 2x = \frac{3\sin 2x - \sin 6x}{4}\), \(\int \sin^3 x \cos^3 x\,dx = \frac{1}{32}\int(3\sin 2x - \sin 6x)\,dx = \frac{1}{32}\left(-\frac{3\cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\cos 6x}{6}\right) + C = -\frac{3\cos 2x}{64} + \frac{\cos 6x}{192} + C\).

Pair \(\sin x \sin 3x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 2x - \cos 4x)\), so \(\sin x \sin 2x \sin 3x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x(\cos 2x - \cos 4x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sin 2x \cos 2x - \sin 2x \cos 4x\right)\). With \(\sin 2x \cos 2x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 4x\) and \(\sin 2x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}(\sin 6x - \sin 2x)\), this equals \(\frac{1}{4}(\sin 4x - \sin 6x + \sin 2x)\). Then \(\int \sin x \sin 2x \sin 3x\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left(-\frac{\cos 4x}{4} + \frac{\cos 6x}{6} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2}\right) + C = \frac{\cos 6x}{24} - \frac{\cos 4x}{16} - \frac{\cos 2x}{8} + C\).

Use \(\sin A \sin B = \frac{1}{2}\left[\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B)\right]\): \(\sin 4x \sin 8x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 4x - \cos 12x)\). Then \(\int \sin 4x \sin 8x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\sin 4x}{4} - \frac{\sin 12x}{12}\right) + C = \frac{\sin 4x}{8} - \frac{\sin 12x}{24} + C\).

Using \(1 - \cos x = 2\sin^2\frac{x}{2}\) and \(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\), \(\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x} = \tan^2\frac{x}{2} = \sec^2\frac{x}{2} - 1\). Then \(\int \frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int\left(\sec^2\frac{x}{2} - 1\right)dx = 2\tan\frac{x}{2} - x + C\).

Write \(\frac{\cos x}{1+\cos x} = \frac{(1+\cos x) - 1}{1+\cos x} = 1 - \frac{1}{1+\cos x}\). Since \(1+\cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\), \(\frac{1}{1+\cos x} = \frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\right)dx = x - \tan\frac{x}{2} + C\).

\(\sin^4 x = \left(\frac{1-\cos 2x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\left(1 - 2\cos 2x + \cos^2 2x\right)\). Replacing \(\cos^2 2x = \frac{1+\cos 4x}{2}\) gives \(\sin^4 x = \frac{3}{8} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\cos 4x}{8}\). Then \(\int \sin^4 x\,dx = \frac{3x}{8} - \frac{\sin 2x}{4} + \frac{\sin 4x}{32} + C\).

\(\cos^4 2x = \left(\frac{1+\cos 4x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\left(1 + 2\cos 4x + \cos^2 4x\right)\). Using \(\cos^2 4x = \frac{1+\cos 8x}{2}\) gives \(\cos^4 2x = \frac{3}{8} + \frac{\cos 4x}{2} + \frac{\cos 8x}{8}\). Then \(\int \cos^4 2x\,dx = \frac{3x}{8} + \frac{\sin 4x}{8} + \frac{\sin 8x}{64} + C\).
Since \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x = (1-\cos x)(1+\cos x)\), \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{1+\cos x} = 1 - \cos x\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin^2 x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int(1 - \cos x)\,dx = x - \sin x + C\).

Using \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\) and \(\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1\), the numerator \(\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha = 2(\cos^2 x - \cos^2\alpha) = 2(\cos x - \cos\alpha)(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\). Hence \(\frac{\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha}{\cos x - \cos\alpha} = 2(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\). Then \(\int 2(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\,dx = 2\sin x + 2x\cos\alpha + C\).

Note \(1 + \sin 2x = \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x + 2\sin x \cos x = (\sin x + \cos x)^2\). Put \(t = \sin x + \cos x\), so \(dt = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{1+\sin 2x}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t^2} = -\frac{1}{t} + C = -\frac{1}{\sin x + \cos x} + C\).

Write \(\tan^3 2x \sec 2x = \tan^2 2x(\sec 2x \tan 2x) = (\sec^2 2x - 1)\sec 2x \tan 2x\). Put \(t = \sec 2x\), so \(dt = 2\sec 2x \tan 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int (\sec^2 2x - 1)\sec 2x \tan 2x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int(t^2 - 1)\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{t^3}{3} - t\right) + C = \frac{\sec^3 2x}{6} - \frac{\sec 2x}{2} + C\).

\(\tan^4 x = \tan^2 x(\sec^2 x - 1) = \tan^2 x \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = \tan^2 x \sec^2 x - (\sec^2 x - 1)\). Since \(\int \tan^2 x \sec^2 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3}\), \(\int \tan^4 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3} - \tan x + x + C\).

Split the fraction: \(\frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} = \sec x \tan x + \csc x \cot x\). Then \(\int(\sec x \tan x + \csc x \cot x)\,dx = \sec x - \csc x + C\).
Since \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\), the numerator \(\cos 2x + 2\sin^2 x = 1\). Hence \(\frac{\cos 2x + 2\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x\). Then \(\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x + C\).

Since \(\sin x \cos^3 x = \tan x \cos^4 x = \frac{\tan x}{\sec^4 x}\), we have \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos^3 x} = \frac{\sec^4 x}{\tan x} = \frac{(1+\tan^2 x)\sec^2 x}{\tan x}\). Put \(t = \tan x\), \(dt = \sec^2 x\,dx\): \(\int \frac{1+t^2}{t}\,dt = \int\left(\frac{1}{t} + t\right)dt = \log|t| + \frac{t^2}{2} + C = \log|\tan x| + \frac{\tan^2 x}{2} + C\).

Since \(\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = (\cos x - \sin x)(\cos x + \sin x)\), \(\frac{\cos 2x}{(\cos x + \sin x)^2} = \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\). Put \(t = \cos x + \sin x\), so \(dt = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C = \log|\cos x + \sin x| + C\).

Write \(\cos x = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\), so \(\sin^{-1}(\cos x) = \frac{\pi}{2} - x\) (taking the principal value, valid for \(0 \le x \le \pi\)). Then \(\int \sin^{-1}(\cos x)\,dx = \int\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)dx = \frac{\pi x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{2} + C\).
_note: Ex 7.3 Q21: sin^{-1}(cos x) reduces to the linear function pi/2 - x only on the principal-value interval 0<=x<=pi; answer given for that intended range (NCERT convention).

solution: Multiply and divide by \(\sin(a-b)\), and use \(\sin(a-b) = \sin\big[(x-b)-(x-a)\big]\). Since \(\frac{\sin[(x-b)-(x-a)]}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \tan(x-b) - \tan(x-a)\), we get \(\frac{1}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[\tan(x-b) - \tan(x-a)\big]\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[-\log|\cos(x-b)| + \log|\cos(x-a)|\big] + C = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\log\left|\frac{\cos(x-a)}{\cos(x-b)}\right| + C\).

Write the numerator as \(\sin x = \sin\big[(x-a)+a\big] = \sin(x-a)\cos a + \cos(x-a)\sin a\). Dividing by \(\sin(x-a)\), \(\frac{\sin x}{\sin(x-a)} = \cos a + \sin a\,\frac{\cos(x-a)}{\sin(x-a)}\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin(x-a)}\,dx = x\cos a + \sin a\,\log|\sin(x-a)| + C\).

Factor the numerator: \(\sin^8 x - \cos^8 x = (\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x)(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x)\). Now \(\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x = (\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = -\cos 2x\), and \(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x \cos^2 x\), which is exactly the denominator. Hence the integrand \(= -\cos 2x\), and \(\int -\cos 2x\,dx = -\frac{\sin 2x}{2} + C\).

Multiply and divide by \(\sin(a-b)\), using \(\sin(a-b) = \sin\big[(x+a)-(x+b)\big]\). Since \(\frac{\sin[(x+a)-(x+b)]}{\cos(x+a)\cos(x+b)} = \tan(x+a) - \tan(x+b)\), we have \(\frac{1}{\cos(x+a)\cos(x+b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[\tan(x+a) - \tan(x+b)\big]\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\cos(x+a)\cos(x+b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[-\log|\cos(x+a)| + \log|\cos(x+b)|\big] + C = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\log\left|\frac{\cos(x+b)}{\cos(x+a)}\right| + C\).

Use \(\sin^3 x = \frac{3\sin x - \sin 3x}{4}\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left[-3\cos x + \frac{\cos 3x}{3}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\). At \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\): \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0,\ \cos\frac{3\pi}{2} = 0\), giving \(0\). At \(x = 0\): \(\frac{1}{4}\left[-3 + \frac{1}{3}\right] = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\left(-\frac{8}{3}\right) = -\frac{2}{3}\). Hence the value is \(0 - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\).

Write \(\tan^3 x = \tan x(\sec^2 x - 1) = \tan x \sec^2 x - \tan x\), so \(\int \tan^3 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^2 x}{2} - \log|\sec x|\). Hence \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} 2\tan^3 x\,dx = \left[\tan^2 x - 2\log|\sec x|\right]_{0}^{\pi/4}\). At \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\): \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1,\ \sec\frac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}\), giving \(1 - 2\log\sqrt{2} = 1 - \log 2\). At \(x = 0\): \(0 - 0 = 0\). Therefore the value is \(1 - \log 2\).
